answers: All 31 siblings of the H13 vtable are vtables for the same value: the 8-byte tagged std io error.  Every header reads size 8 / align 8 and every one of the 30 distinct drop bodies is the same tag-dispatch template (tag & 3; only tag 1 acts, dropping the boxed inner error through its own vtable and freeing the 24-byte box via 0x64df4a0).

18 of the 32 are standalone Debug-only vtables (extent 0x20); 13 are extended vtables (extent 0x58) whose slots are the Debug stub, the Display body 0x5ca84b0, a pointer to the one-method Display vtable at base-0x20, the +0x30 and +0x48 forwarders 0x5ca8760 / 0x5ca8730, and three local bodies; 1 (tokio 0x64c6458, extent 0x40) carries four local slots instead.

The 94 references are all rip-relative lea: 57 panic-pair sites (messages and Locations pinned per site, from 'failed to spawn thread' expects to tokio's 'failed to wake I/O driver' and libstd's own internal unwraps on 0x64c3270), 6 field accessors and 10 enum accessors returning (value, vtable) pairs out of parent trait objects, 14 pair-store and 3 clone sites, and 4 other sites.
limitations: Parent traits of the accessor, store and clone bodies are recorded structurally (parent vtable, entry offset, Self size and drop) but not named; the byte evidence does not carry trait names.
The extended vtables' local slots (+0x38, +0x40, +0x50) and tokio vtable 0x64c6458's four local slots are recorded as targets; the traits they serve are not identified.
The forwarders at +0x30 and +0x48 are pinned by their forwarding targets inside the boxed error's vtable; their trait-slot names are not asserted.
Panic messages and Locations are read from the static string and Location records the bodies load; no value was executed.
